title: Work IQ: agents upload files and content to Microsoft 365
summary: Hold: the briefing treats Work IQ's documented user-permission boundary as unconfirmed and overstates which permission applications need for writes. The roadmap facts and admin path are accurate, but the overwrite claim lacks evidence and Microsoft's differing descriptions of write defaults should be acknowledged.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation says mutation operations are blocked by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: After this statement add: 'The Work IQ in Copilot Studio page separately says write operations are on by default, subject to organisational permissions and policies; Microsoft does not reconcile these descriptions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq.

claims.claim: Work IQ requests run in the context of a signed-in user.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: SharePoint Tools OAuth scopes do not grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing SharePoint permissions.
claims.quote: OAuth scopes don't grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing SharePoint permissions.

claims.claim: Whether the signed-in-user permission boundary applies to Work IQ upload is not stated.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether the same limit applies to this upload capability is not stated.' with 'The Work IQ overview states that every request runs in a user's context and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.' The platform-wide boundary already covers Work IQ requests; retain the separate uncertainty about supported destinations.

claims.claim: Apps need WorkIQ.Act to change Microsoft 365 data through Work IQ.
claims.quote: Allows the app to ask Work IQ agents questions and receive responses on behalf of the signed-in user. This includes read and write access to Microsoft 365 resources that are accessible to Work IQ agents and scoped to the signed-in user.
claims.fix: Replace 'Apps need the `WorkIQ.Act` scope to change Microsoft 365 data through Work IQ' with 'For SharePoint Tools, Microsoft documents `WorkIQ.Act` for actions that change SharePoint content or configuration'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/sharepoint-iq. Keep the existing statement that WorkIQ.Act requires admin consent; do not imply it is the only Work IQ permission permitting writes.
